text:
Alex: FYI I'm handing off oncall to @Maria G for the next 48h. Quick notes and a few clarifying Qs below.

Alex: Current risks — two low-level consumer queue retries are elevated but stable, and a recent rollout was reverted yesterday. No active incidents.

Alex: Handoff checklist (quick):
```
- Check Prod job queue health (metrics: job_latency, job_backlog)
- Verify orchestration workers >= min_pool (3)
- Confirm redis replication healthy
- Confirm canary fallback policy set for model-variant X
```

Maria G: thanks — noted. For clarity, can we agree on what qualifies as an "incident" vs a "product degradation" here? I want to avoid escalations we don't need.

Kevin S: short answer — incident = service/unavailable or violates SLA thresholds (e.g., 5xx spikes > 1% sustained for 5m, p50 latency beyond target for majority of requests). Degradation = increased latency or error rate that doesn't cross SLA and has mitigations in place.

Jamie: adding ops nuance — if customers are reporting inability to generate or high rate-limited failures impacting production, treat as incident and escalate. If it's internal jobs/backfill delays, treat as degradation unless it impacts live traffic.

Alex: escalation paths: first oncall (Maria) -> page SRE lead (Kevin) if it's an incident per Kevin's definition -> loop in runtime eng (Jamie) for model/runtime-specific failures -> exec escalation only if customer SLA risk.

Maria G: for paging thresholds, are we using the same PD policies? pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty policy: "prod-service"
- P1: page immediately if 5xx > 2% for 3m or 95th latency > 2x SLA for 5m
- P2: notify if error rate between 0.5% and 2% for 10m

Kevin S: yes that's current. Also, runtime team owns any model-serving runtime faults (OOMs, GPU crashes, model load failures). SRE owns infra-level (k8s node flapping, network partition, disk full, DB failover). If it's ambiguous (e.g., GPU OOM triggered by model config), page both and set triage channel.

Alex: practical example: model tokenization failure leading to 400s — runtime owns (model input path). If pods crash across nodes due to kubelet bug, SRE owns.

Jamie: handshake: when runtime owns, we still expect SRE to help with cross-cluster networking and node-level debugging. Runtime will own rollbacks, model config patches, and model-specific metrics.

Maria G: ok, last Q: any special runbook links for canary fallback and circuit-breakers? Alex, can you paste the runbook?

Alex: pasted runbook snippet:
```
- Runbook: docs/runbooks/oncall/fallbacks.md
- Steps: 1) Check canary health dashboard 2) Flip router fallback to variant Y 3) Monitor for 10m 4) Roll forward if healthy
```

Maria G: perfect. I'll monitor dashboards and ping if anything crosses PD P1. Thanks for the handoff notes. :thumbsup:

Kevin S: thanks, @Maria G. If anything smells like infrastructure, ping me directly. :eyes:

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: oncall shift started for Maria G — escalation policy: prod-service (P1).

Jamie: one more housekeeping — I'll post a short postmortem template in #eng-oncall for any degradations we decide to classify as incidents.

Alex: thanks all — leaving a short doc in the handoffs folder too. Good luck! :v:
